source: Belfield, S. and Brown, C. (2010). Guidebook on Upland Crops in Cambodia: Corn (សៀវភៅណែនាំ ស្តីពីដំណាំតំបន់ខ្ពង់រាបនៅក្នុងប្រទេសកម្ពុជា៖ ដំណាំពោត). ACIAR Monograph 143, published by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in partnership with NSW Department of Primary Industries, the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI), Murdoch University, University of Canberra, and MAFF, under ACIAR Project ASEM/2000/109. Uploaded PDF, 52 pages, image-only (Limon-font-era scan, read via page rasterization).
text:
Corn development is commonly described using a staging system with vegetative stages (V) counted by leaf number, and reproductive stages (R) after flowering. The source presents a growth-stage chart (adapted from NSW Department of Primary Industries) covering: VE (emergence), V2, V5, V8, V12, V16 (vegetative stages, roughly corresponding to plant heights of about 0, 10, 30, 60 cm and increasing further through V12-V16), R1 (silking, roughly 75 cm+ and about 60 days after emergence in the chart), and R5 (dent stage, around 100 days after emergence, close to full height of roughly 270 cm).

Note on precision: the chart gives approximate days-after-emergence and heights for each stage (VE at 0 days; V2 at about 7 days; V5 at about 18 days; V8 at about 28 days; V12 at about 42 days; V16 at about 56 days; R1 at about 75 days; R5 at about 100 days), but exact timing varies with variety, temperature, and growing conditions, so these should be treated as general guides rather than fixed schedules for a particular field.
